clue.text: Trade on offers supplied by Shakespearean scene

indicators.note: made supple, so the letters of these three words are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A merchant's bargains are provided by a setting from one of the Bard's plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supplied' is read as 'made supple': the thirteen letters of TRADE ON OFFERS are loosened and rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Forest of Arden is the woodland setting of As You Like It, a famous Shakespearean location.

clue.text: Bloomer reported by Dario and Dad?

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: the dramatist Dario Fo and his father: Fo's pa

explanation.surface: A howler apparently relayed by an Italian playwright and his father.
explanation.walkthrough: Dario Fo was an Italian Nobel-winning playwright; his dad is 'Fo's pa', which said out loud is the French phrase for a social slip.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a blunder, the same as an embarrassing social mistake or gaffe.

clue.text: Half-Welsh 1 across with two circular lines

indicators.note: taking half of the forest's name keeps just its first three of six letters

parts.note: Radnor Forest is in mid-Wales
II is two in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Part of a Welsh woodland comes with a pair of round lines.
explanation.walkthrough: Clues reading '1 across' stand for 'forest': here the Welsh one, Radnor Forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Radii are the straight lines drawn from the centre of a circle to its edge, so lines belonging to a circle.

clue.text: Swimmer holds back information in Africa

indicators.note: the swimmer is said to clasp the next piece inside its body

parts.note: a seal is a swimming marine mammal

indicators.note: the word for information is to be taken backwards

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A creature of the sea keeps facts to itself somewhere on the African continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the information word round before the swimmer holds it. 'Swimmer' tempts toward fish such as EEL, but a marine mammal is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Senegal is a country on the west coast of the African continent.

clue.text: Take one voice in Venice

parts.note: R abbreviates Latin recipe, 'take', at the head of prescriptions
I is the Roman numeral one
alto is a singing voice

explanation.surface: A tourist told to pick a singer while visiting the Italian city of canals.
explanation.walkthrough: R for 'take' comes from the recipe sign on old prescriptions.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto is the famous bridge and market district of Venice, so something found in that city.

clue.text: Singular French firm stifling a touch of class — it points downwards

indicators.note: to stifle is to smother, so these outer letters wrap round what follows

parts.note: ICI, Imperial Chemical Industries, was a major British company
le is the French singular definite article

indicators.note: only a tiny part, the opening letter, of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A one-off company from France is suppressing a hint of style in something that hangs down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singular French firm' reads as one company, but it splits into a British firm and the French article, with the touch of class between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An icicle hangs from eaves with its tapering tip pointing to the ground.

clue.text: Drink causes prisoner to make mistake about buzzer

parts.note: lag is slang for a convict, as in 'old lag'

indicators.note: the mistake word goes round the buzzing insect

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake
a bee is an insect that buzzes

explanation.surface: Alcohol leads a convict to blunder over a noisy insect.
explanation.walkthrough: The buzzing insect splits the mistake word after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager beer is a pale bottom-fermented beverage, a kind of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: See 1 across
Having a stud of a sort in a singular article of clothing

indicators.note: the type word is placed inside the garment

parts.note: a stocking, one of a pair of hosiery items
a breed is a sort or variety of animal

explanation.surface: Wearing a stud earring of some kind with one odd garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singular' points to one of a pair: one stocking rather than stockings. 'stud' looks like jewellery but means a horse-breeding establishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockbreeding is the raising of livestock, the business of someone who keeps a stud of animals.

clue.text: Money to chew?

definitions.meaning: British slang for a pound sterling
a lump of tobacco held in the mouth and chewed

explanation.definitionFit: Quid means both a pound coin and a plug of chewing tobacco, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Sir John and Sir Bernard served Thatcher with a 1 across

parts.note: Sir John Nott was Margaret Thatcher's Defence Secretary
Sir Bernard Ingham was Margaret Thatcher's press secretary

explanation.surface: Two knights who worked for the Iron Lady come with some woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a city that comes with a forest: Nottingham Forest is its football club, and Sherwood Forest lies nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Joined to the word forest, the city's name gives Nottingham Forest, the famous football club, so it is a place paired with one.

clue.text: 1 across to peg out and peg in?

indicators.note: here means awry or disordered, so the letters of the first peg are shaken up

parts.note: to pin something is to fix it in place with a peg

explanation.surface: A woodland where one may fix a tent peg out and then drive one in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' scrambles PEG, and its letters join PIN ('peg in') in a single mix to make the forest's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Epping Forest is an ancient woodland on the north-east edge of London.

clue.text: Depression or trouble caused by beetle?

parts.note: a col is a dip or pass between mountain peaks
taken as written
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: Asking whether some low mood or difficulty was brought on by an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: the word completes 'Colorado beetle', the potato pest.
explanation.definitionFit: Colorado is the first word of the Colorado beetle, a striped pest of potato crops.

clue.text: Old instrument for a walk without L-Lincoln

indicators.note: the named letter is dropped from the word for a walk

parts.note: a stroll is a leisurely walk
Abe was the nickname of US President Abraham Lincoln

explanation.surface: An antique device used for an outing that leaves a stammering president behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter 'L-Lincoln' supplies the L to remove from STROLL.
explanation.definitionFit: An astrolabe was an early instrument for measuring the altitude of stars, used by navigators and astronomers.

clue.text: Where a dog is concerned, payment is continually cropping up

parts.note: re means concerning and a cur is a dog
rent is a regular payment for property

explanation.surface: When it comes to a mutt, the bills just keep arriving.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the crossword staple for 'about' or 'concerning'.
explanation.definitionFit: Recurrent describes something happening again and again, repeatedly cropping up.

clue.text: Ecclesiastical 1 across?

parts.note: a woodland that shares its name with a senior cathedral cleric, read as a church forest

explanation.definitionFit: The Forest of Dean in Gloucestershire bears the title of a church official who heads a cathedral chapter.

clue.text: Chief of the Star Chamber

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: The head of the notorious Tudor court that sat in secret.
explanation.walkthrough: The Star Chamber was an English court abolished in 1641; the four letters straddle its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch as an adjective means chief or principal, as in archenemy.

clue.text: 1 across tree felled

parts.note: the ash is a common tree
something felled has been knocked or cut down

explanation.surface: A woodland where a tree has been chopped.
explanation.walkthrough: Ashdown Forest in Sussex is the setting of the Winnie-the-Pooh stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashdown Forest is an area of heath and woodland in East Sussex.

clue.text: Oarsman on island has a go on a typewriter

indicators.note: in a down-style placement the rower comes after the island

parts.note: a key is a low island, as in the Florida Keys
the stroke is the rower who sets the pace in a crew

explanation.surface: A rower stranded on an islet has a try at typing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down-light-style reading, 'on' puts the rower after the island.
explanation.definitionFit: A keystroke is a single press of a typewriter or keyboard key, one go at it.

clue.text: Chief is wrestling before coming in

indicators.note: the word for 'before' enters the wrestling word

parts.note: sumo is Japanese wrestling
pre is a prefix meaning before

explanation.surface: The boss is grappling until someone enters the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link; the surface's wrestler 'coming in' to the ring hides the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A supremo is the person in overall charge, a boss or chief.

clue.text: 1 across is red, like revolutionary

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns things over, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woodland described as red, much like a radical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like a noun for a red but rearranges RED and LIKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Kielder Forest in Northumberland is one of the largest planted forests in England.

clue.text: Woodworker doesn't want to be left out

definitions.text: doesn't want to be left out
definitions.meaning: someone who joins clubs and groups

explanation.definitionFit: A joiner is both a carpenter of fittings and a person who habitually joins societies.

clue.text: 1 across taken to court in the case of the pottery fragment

indicators.note: the courting word goes inside, as if in a case made of the fragment

parts.note: a sherd is a broken piece of pottery
to woo is to court

explanation.surface: A wood brought to a law court over a broken bit of crockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the case of' sounds legal but means WOO is encased in SHERD.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherwood Forest in Nottinghamshire is the legendary home of Robin Hood.

clue.text: New 1 across features 25 9s

definitions.meaning: the wild horses that roam the New Forest in Hampshire
a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds, so twenty-five quids

explanation.definitionFit: New Forest ponies are a famous breed, and in slang a pony is a sum of twenty-five pounds.

clue.text: Brief last greeting sounds noble

indicators.note: tells us the word for a noble is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: a knight is a titled noble

explanation.surface: A short farewell at bedtime resembles an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' shortens 'goodnight' to 'night, said at the day's end.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Night is a clipped form of goodnight, the parting greeting before bed.

clue.text: "The old order changeth" can never go

indicators.note: the archaic word for changes tells us the following letters alter their order

explanation.surface: Quoting Tennyson's line, a stubborn regime insists it will never depart.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is from Tennyson's Morte d'Arthur. 'changeth' applies to CAN NEVER GO, rearranging its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Governance means rule or control, an older word for the order by which something is run.

clue.text: See 26
Character at the gallery such as Aeolus and his like

definitions.text: such as Aeolus and his like

parts.note: nature is a person's character
the gods is the highest gallery in a theatre

explanation.surface: A personality up in the cheap theatre seats.
explanation.walkthrough: THE GODS is British slang for the top balcony seats of a theatre. Aeolus was the Greek keeper of the winds.
explanation.definitionFit: Aeolus, ruler of the winds, is an example of deities who personify natural forces.

clue.text: Nurse or doctor 1 across

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the forest word is altered

parts.note: the cross-reference stands for the word forest

explanation.surface: A carer or a physician of the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a noun alongside 'Nurse' but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To foster is to nurse or nurture, as in fostering hopes or a child.
